sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2065432100 — Canary cluster (cluster-canary-eu) reporting 95th p90/p95 latency jump and increased timeouts. Auto-remediation attempted: traffic-shift -> partial.
Jordan Lee: seeing 3x p95 on canary hosts, tails up to ~4s, throughput dropping. Noticed kernel fallback counts rising in telemetry.
Maya Patel: on it. which rollout?
Jordan Lee: rollout_id=rl-2026-03-15-9b3, feature=continuous_batch_v2, started ~20m ago.
Li Chen: paging in case it's related to kernel selection fallback — kernel_fallback_rate went from 0.5% -> 12% on canary nodes.
Jamie R: maybe quantized kernel got selected under longer sequences, batching logic miscalculated. Logs show KV cache eviction spikes right before fallback.
Jordan Lee: customer impact? any 5xxs?
Ops Runbook: Some requests are timing out (deadline exceeded) and a small percent (0.6%) 500s from runtime. Most are high-latency returns. Affected routes: /v1/generate chat endpoints primarily in EU region.
Maya Patel: ok first mitigation plan: pause rollout, flip feature flag to previous, remove canary traffic from new pool. Jordan, Li, can you run the flag flip?
Jordan Lee: running `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags/continuous_batch_v2 -d '{"enabled":false}'` -> got 200. Posting output:```{"flag":"continuous_batch_v2","previous":true,"updated":false,"actor":"oncall","ts":"2026-03-15T10:12:03Z"}```
Li Chen: good. Also draining canary pool rl-2026-03-15-9b3. `rbctl traffic shift --from rl-2026-03-15-9b3 --to stable --percent 100` executed.
Jamie R: I see kernel fallback count drop on one host after drain, but another host still showing latent KV cache thrashing. Might need to restart runtime on that host to clear caches.
Maya Patel: agree. Jordan, schedule rolling restart on the stuck host group and set affinity to prefer standard kernels. Use `infra-restart --group canary-eu-2 --service runtime --post-hook \"trace-check\"`
Jordan Lee: kicking off restart now. Should take ~3-4 minutes per host.
Ops Runbook: Notifying customers: small subset in EU may have experienced degraded latency; posting status page update: \"Investigating elevated latency for EU generation endpoints. We have paused the rollout and are mitigating; no major data loss expected.\"
Maya Patel: monitoring metrics — p95 trending down from 3.8s -> 1.2s after flag flip + host restarts. Throughput returning to normal but still seeing a 0.1% residual error.
Li Chen: found related stack traces: `runtime/kernel_selector.cc` falling back due to `kernel_compat_check()` false for continuous_batch_v2 path when sequence_length > 2048. There's also an eviction NOTE in KV cache logs: `kv_cache_eviction: high_pressure` right before tail spike.
Jordan Lee: is the rollback of the rollout complete? traffic reports 100% to stable now.
Jamie R: yes RL drained fully. Verified by `rbctl status rl-2026-03-15-9b3` -> `state: drained`.
Maya Patel: decision log: rollback rollout rl-2026-03-15-9b3, flip continuous_batch_v2=false, mark as blocked until kernel compatibility fix and additional canary tests.
Ops Runbook: Customer impact estimate: ~0.4% of requests in EU saw >2s latency, <0.01% saw 5xx. Affected customers flagged for outreach if they reached error thresholds.
Jordan Lee: creating post-incident ticket and tagging release engineering + runtime-ml. Root suspects: kernel selector false negative for certain long sequences, combined with aggressive KV cache policy under new batching path.
Li Chen: suggested next steps: 1) revert canary config as done, 2) add extra pre-flight kernel compatibility checks in rollout pipeline, 3) add cache pressure circuit breaker (throttle batch expansion when eviction rate>X), 4) increase canary observation window for sequencing.
Jamie R: I'll open PR with a delta to kernel_selector to log more context and soft-fail earlier (graceful degrade to stable kernel instead of full fallback).
Maya Patel: handoff — I'm going offline in 15. Jordan you're on for next 2 hours. Tagging @Jordan Lee for post-incident follow-ups and customer comms.
Jordan Lee: noted. Scheduling 1hr follow-up call in 30m to review telemetry and confirm stable.
Ops Runbook: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Will update status page to \"mitigated, investigating root cause\" and follow up with customers if any residual errors persist. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: thanks team. Postmortem owner assigned: Jamie R. Please include timeline, telemetry snapshots, and action items (kernel selector fix, cache breaker, rollout gating).
Jamie R: will do. Adding owners and ETA in the ticket.
sre-bot: Incident 2065432100 status changed to MONITORING by Jordan Lee at 2026-03-15T10:23:45Z
Jordan Lee: closing thread here, will reopen if we see a regression.
